Scope and method

All 83 corrected English names, displayed credentials, fields, titles/affiliations, and biographies were reread. The active chunk files, monolithic fallback, and Deployment copies were checked for agreement. The unused legacy mapping i18n/scientists-profiles-en.json was excluded. Credential codes are rendered by the site and were preserved.

American English is retained. Official names, transliterations, dates, figures, and factual claims have not been normalized by inference. Verification items require authoritative clarification; this is a language review, not external fact-checking. Entries already covered by a carried-over question are not duplicated as new findings.

Source validation checked JSON parsing, synchronized copies, unchanged HTML tag sequences, unchanged numeric values, and changes confined to the approved English fields. The rollback patch passed a reverse-application check. Browser visual preview was unavailable; the report was checked structurally.

Before

<p class="bio bio-lead">Aytekin Huseynli is an international specialist in social policy, social work, child and family welfare. Dr. Huseynli is an assistant professor at the University of Washington. Her applied research focuses on the formulation of social policies, especially the improvement of family and child welfare. Aytekin Huseynli also explores strategies and ways to channel natural resource revenues into social development in countries rich in oil, gas and minerals. Aytekin Huseynli&#x27;s doctoral dissertation led to the creation of the National Children&#x27;s Fund state program, which covers 7 million children in Kazakhstan and is financed by a portion of the oil and gas wealth.</p><p class="bio">She is the author of 3 chapters in 3 books in the field of social policy, social work and social development, 15 scientific articles in 15 international scientific journals, and more than 20 publications, and she is a member of the editorial board of 2 scientific journals in the field of social development, social policy and social work. She gave presentations at more than 20 international scientific conferences and received 2 international awards for her scientific work. She was the scientific supervisor of more than 10 students. Aytekin Huseynli teaches social research, statistics, program evaluation and social policy. Currently, she is the head of several research projects.</p><p class="bio">A pioneer in her field, Aytekin Huseynli is one of the first professional social workers who received an education in the field of social work in the post-Soviet region and is one of the founders of the social work profession and education in Azerbaijan. She is the founder of the "Azerbaijan Social Work" Public Union, which represents Azerbaijan in the field of international and regional social development.</p><p class="bio">She is a member of the Board of Directors of the Global Program at the Brown School of the University of Washington, the deputy director of international programs at the Center for Social Development, and an associate professor at the Center for Child Abuse Research, Training and Education. At the global level, Aytekin Huseynli is a research and statistics specialist for Eurasia at UNICEF and a member of the Research Committee of the International Association of Schools of Social Work.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">Sevinj Mammadova is a very experienced specialist in the field of education policy. She specializes in the development and implementation of strategies aimed at improving education systems. Sevinj Mammadova has led large-scale international projects to increase the quality and accessibility of education and ensure that every person who wants to study gets equal opportunities, resources and support, regardless of their background, socioeconomic status, gender, ethnicity and other factors. Her work aims to make education systems more effective and align them more closely with national priorities.</p><p class="bio">Sevinj Mammadova has extensive skills in managing large-scale projects, ensuring efficient use of resources, and making important decisions that improve educational outcomes. She involves key stakeholders such as teachers, students and government representatives in the decision-making process and actively participates in defining long-term educational goals.</p><p class="bio">Sevinj Mammadova holds a Ph.D. in Educational Management and Strategies, which further strengthens her ability to lead and recommend educational reforms. <p class="bio bio-lead">With the support of the "2007–2015 State Program for the Education of Azerbaijani Youth in Foreign Countries," he completed his doctorate with honors at the Mannheim Medical Faculty of Heidelberg University. His main research focus is the creation of complex 3D cell cultures in vitro for the study of tumor diseases and the investigation of the effect of tumor cells on drugs in those cultures through various biomarkers. The findings of this research have been published in two peer-reviewed articles so far. The most recent article was highly appreciated by the journal &quot;Frontiers in Oncology&quot; and republished in a special issue. In addition, the program he wrote for the segmentation of large-volume confocal microscopic images is currently in the process of being registered as an invention. As a group leader, he supervises 2 master's students and 1 doctoral student.</p>

After

<p class="bio bio-lead">Dr. Vahid Garousi works in two professional roles: as an IT specialist and an IT professor. Since 1998 he has provided consulting and training to international IT companies in software engineering, testing and QA, and he is also a professor of software engineering at Queen&#x27;s University in Belfast, United Kingdom. At the same time, he serves as a part-time Software Test Strategist and Team Leader at ProSys LLC in Azerbaijan and Testinium A.Ş. in Turkey. His name is written in English as Vahid Garousi.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Garousi earned his Ph.D. in Software Engineering from Carleton University in Canada in 2006 and his master&#x27;s degree from the University of Waterloo in Canada in 2003. Over more than 25 years of IT experience, he served as the lead test and QA consultant for the United Kingdom&#x27;s COVID mobile application in 2020–2021, as a test consultant for one of the UK&#x27;s major banks in 2022, and as the lead test and QA consultant at HAVELSAN in Turkey from 2012 to 2019.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Garousi is a professor of software engineering at Queen&#x27;s University in Belfast, United Kingdom. Previously he held associate professor positions in the Netherlands (2017–2019), Turkey (2015–2017) and Canada (2001–2014). He received his Ph.D. in Software Engineering from Carleton University in Canada in 2006. His research areas are software engineering, software testing, empirical studies, action research and industry–academia collaboration. In parallel with his academic career, he is a practicing consultant and trainer in software engineering, delivering consulting and corporate training across various areas including software engineering, testing and quality assurance, model-driven development and software maintenance.</p><p class="bio">In a bibliometric study published in the Journal of Systems and Software in 2018, Dr. Garousi was ranked the 8th most active mid-career software engineering researcher in the world, out of more than 4,000 active researchers. Dr. Garousi has published more than 150 papers to date. He was selected as a Distinguished Speaker by the IEEE Computer Society in 2012–2015. He is also a member of the IEEE and the IEEE Computer Society and a licensed professional engineer (PEng) in Alberta, Canada.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Garousi has been the principal investigator of several research projects and has launched many significant R&amp;D software engineering projects together with software companies in several countries, including Canada and Turkey. He has served as an organizer and program committee member at many international conferences, such as ICST, ICSP, CSEE&amp;T, MoDELS and the Turkish National Software Engineering Conference. Among the awards he has received is the Alberta Ingenuity New Faculty Award, which he won in 2007.</p><p class="bio-section-title">Scientific achievements and recognition:</p><div Previously he held associate professor positions in the Netherlands (2017–2019), Turkey (2015–2017) and Canada (2001–2014). He received his Ph.D. in software engineering from Carleton University in Canada in 2006. His research areas are software engineering, software testing, empirical studies, action research and industry–academia collaboration. In parallel with his academic career, he is a practicing consultant and trainer in software engineering, delivering consulting and corporate training across various areas including software engineering, testing and quality assurance, model-driven development and software maintenance.</p><p class="bio">In a bibliometric study published in the Journal of Systems and Software in 2018, Dr. Garousi was ranked the 8th most active mid-career software engineering researcher in the world, out of more than 4,000 active researchers. Dr. Garousi has published more than 150 papers to date. He was selected as a Distinguished Speaker by the IEEE Computer Society in 2012–2015. He is also a member of the IEEE and the IEEE Computer Society and a licensed professional engineer (PEng) in Alberta, Canada.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Garousi has been the principal investigator of several research projects and has launched many significant R&amp;D software engineering projects together with software companies in several countries, including Canada and Turkey. He has served as an organizer and program committee member at many international conferences, such as ICST, ICSP, CSEE&amp;T, MoDELS and the Turkish National Software Engineering Conference. Among the awards he has received is the Alberta Ingenuity New Faculty Award, which he won in 2007.</p><p class="bio-section-title">Scientific achievements and recognition:</p><div <p class="bio">Khagani Gayibli is a poet, translator, scholar and public figure. In addition to his extensive research in Azerbaijani literature, linguistics and journalism, he is also known internationally for diaspora activity and academic cooperation. With his scientific work "Comparison of Verb Structures in Estonian and Turkish Languages," he is the first Azerbaijani scholar to investigate kinship relations between Finno-Ugric and Turkic-Tatar languages in world linguistics.</p><p class="bio-section-title">Main research areas</p><p class="bio-section-title">Turkology and linguistics:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;Comparison of Verb Structures in Estonian and Turkish Languages&quot;</li><li>&quot;Linguistic relations and structural differences between Turkish and Estonian&quot;</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Political and cultural relations:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;Political and cultural relations between Estonia and the Turkic World&quot;</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Journalism and visual media:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;The importance of photography in the print media&quot;</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Awards and honorary titles:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;Progress&quot; medal (2022) – awarded by the President of Azerbaijan for his contribution to the development of the Azerbaijani diaspora.</li><li>&quot;Golden Star Medal&quot; (2024) – awarded by the International Academy of Sciences for Turkic World Studies of the Republic of Turkey.</li><li>Medal &quot;For service in diaspora activity&quot; (2024) – presented by the State Committee on Work with Diaspora of the Republic of Azerbaijan.</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Publications and literary activity:</p><p class="bio">Khagani Gayibli is the author of both scholarly and journalistic articles and works of poetry and prose. His works have been translated into Estonian, Georgian, Russian, Latvian, German, English and Turkic languages.</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>author of more than 40 sociopolitical, historical and scientific-cultural articles,</li><li>6 books and 1 monograph,</li><li>author of 4 scientific articles published in 2 scientific journals.</li><li>speaker and participant at more than 20 international symposia and conferences.</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Professional and academic activity:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>Finno-Ugric and Turkic Peoples Research Center – chairman</li><li>University of Tartu (Estonia) – director of the Turkish Language Center</li><li>World Congress of Azerbaijanis – member of the Board, deputy chairman</li><li>Estonian-Azerbaijani Society – chairman</li><li>World Association of Azerbaijani Scientists – member of the Organizing Committee</li><li>Azerbaijan Writers&#x27; Union – member</li><li>Estonian Society of Academic Orientalists – member</li><li>Turkish Literature Foundation – honorary member</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Diplomatic and translation activity:</p><p class="bio">Khagani Gayibli has participated as a translator in high-level official meetings in Estonia and Turkey. He served as a special interpreter during official visits by the presidents, parliament speakers and ministers of Azerbaijan, Turkey and Estonia.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">In 2019, she obtained a Ph.D. degree in materials chemistry from the University of Orleans, France. Aynur Guliyeva also has industrial experience - she worked as a project manager for medicinal capsules for 2 years at Capsugel, which is part of the Lonza company. She also performs various teaching and administrative duties at the university and mentors female scientists to support their professional development. Aynur Guliyeva has a number of scientific articles and has made oral and poster presentations at international conferences.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">Honorary professor of Azerbaijan State Oil and Industry University</p><p class="bio">Professor Lev Eppelbaum (Tel Aviv University, Department of Geophysics) is the author of approximately 460 scientific publications. These include 12 books, 18 book chapters, 194 peer-reviewed journal articles, 81 conference materials and 171 abstracts published by international scientific publishers (Kluwer Academic Publisher, Springer, Elsevier, Chapman and Hall, Institute of Physics (Great Britain)). Prof. Eppelbaum&#x27;s main research areas are geodynamics and tectonic reconstructions, applied and environmental geophysics, archaeological geophysics, and integrated analysis of geophysical, geological and related data.</p><p class="bio">He was elected head of scientific departments 26 times at international conferences. Professor Lev Eppelbaum is the editor-in-chief of the journal "Geology, Geophysics, and Earth Sciences" and a member of the editorial boards of such prestigious journals as "Positioning," "Open Petroleum Engineering Journal," "Archaeological Discovery," "Stratigraphy, Petroleum, Sedimentology, Geochemistry," "ANAS Transactions, Earth Sciences," "International Journal of Earthquake Engineering," "Discover Geoscience," "Academy Green Energy," "Contributions to Geosciences," "Geosciences," "Russian Journal of Physical Chemistry," "World Journal of Physics." At the same time, he served as a guest editor for the journals "Advances in Geosciences," "Journal of Geophysics and Engineering," "Continent and Life Evolution," "Frontiers in Earth Sciences," "Geosciences (Switzerland)," &quot;Land&quot; and "Applied Sciences (Switzerland)."</p><p class="bio">Professor Lev Eppelbaum is a member of two international geophysical commissions: &quot;Rotation of the Earth&quot; commission and "WebmedCentral Ecology Advisory Board."</p><p class="bio">In 2020, he was awarded the title of honorary professor of the Azerbaijan State Oil and Industry University, and in 2023, he was elected a foreign member of the Georgian Academy of Sciences.</p><p class="bio">Professor Eppelbaum has received several awards; among them is the Christian Huygens medal of the European Geosciences Union (2019).</p><p class="bio">According to Google Scholar, his scholarly publications have been cited nearly 8,000 times.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">A teacher of Azerbaijani language and literature at the Faculty of Literature of Cairo University, a scientific leader at the department of Oriental languages ​​and Arabic, president of the Egypt-Azerbaijan Peoples&#x27; Friendship Academy, adviser on foreign relations of the General Secretariat of the World Fatwa Organizations, chairman of the Board of the Egypt-Azerbaijan Friendship Society, head of the Azerbaijani Diaspora in Egypt.</p><p class="bio">Since the 2016–2017 academic year, he has been working as a teacher of the Azerbaijani language at the Faculty of Literature of Cairo University, Egypt, and as a scientific supervisor at the department of Oriental Languages ​​and Arabic Language of the faculty. By 2026, he had taught the Azerbaijani language to more than 1,700 Egyptians.</p><p class="bio-section-title">Public and professional activities:</p><ul class="bullets"><li>Founder and president of the Egypt-Azerbaijan Peoples&#x27; Friendship Academy</li><li>Adviser on foreign relations of the General Secretariat of the World Fatwa Institutions</li><li>Chairman of the Board of the Egypt-Azerbaijan Friendship Society</li><li>Head of the Azerbaijani Diaspora in Egypt</li><li>Executive Director of Halga Foundation</li><li>Coordinator of Egypt-Azerbaijan inter-parliamentary friendship group.</li><li>Since 2003, he has led thousands of students from more than 100 countries who came to study in Egypt, and through them he is promoting the truths of Azerbaijan in the world. Currently (in 2025), he is leading more than 2,000 students from 65 countries studying in Egypt.</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Scientific and research activities:</p><p class="bio">For more than 25 years, he has been conducting research on Azerbaijan in Arabic sources. As a result of these studies, he wrote two books in Arabic about more than 250 Azerbaijani scientists.</p><p class="bio">The work &quot;Azerbaijani scientists and writers in Arabic sources&quot; was published in the Azerbaijani language in 2022.</p><p class="bio">He discovered manuscripts of hundreds of Azerbaijani scientists in Egyptian libraries and studied them.</p><p class="bio">More than 15 scientific and journalistic articles were published in Arabic and Azerbaijani languages ​​in prestigious magazines of Arab countries and Azerbaijan.</p><p class="bio-section-title">International activity:</p><p class="bio">He participated in more than 20 international conferences held in different countries of the world and made speeches on scientific and cultural topics related to Azerbaijan.</p><p class="bio-section-title">Awards:</p><div class="awards-block"><ul class="awards-list"><li>In 2017, by order of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Mr. Ilham Aliyev, he was awarded the &quot;Progress&quot; medal for his services in the field of strengthening friendship between peoples and the development of the Azerbaijani diaspora;</li><li>On July 18, 2018, he was awarded the medal of the Egyptian Ministry of Education for his exceptional services in the development of cultural and scientific relations between Egypt and Azerbaijan;</li><li>In 2019, he was honored by the Embassy of Uzbekistan in Egypt for his support to the Uzbek Diaspora living in Egypt;</li><li>In 2019, he was honored by the Trade Union of Seyids in Egypt for his exceptional services in the development of relations between Egypt and Azerbaijan;</li><li>In 2020, he was awarded the medal &quot;For service in diaspora activity&quot; for his great contributions to the diaspora policy of our country;</li><li>In 2024, he received an honorary award by the Union of Arab Countries Students studying at al-Azhar University;</li><li>In 2024, by order of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Mr. Ilham Aliyev, he was awarded the &quot;100th anniversary of Heydar Aliyev&quot; (1923–2023) jubilee medal for his services in implementing the idea of ​​Azerbaijanism and strengthening the solidarity of Azerbaijanis of the world.</li><li>On September 3, 2025, he was awarded the first-class "Science and Sciences" order by the President of Egypt, Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi. Seymur Nasirov is the first person to be awarded this order among foreigners living in Egypt.</li><li>On October 1, 2025, he was awarded the medal of the Ministry of Education of Egypt for his services in the development of scientific and cultural relations between the Arab Republic of Egypt and the Republic of Azerbaijan and was awarded a letter of appreciation by the Egyptian Cultural Center in Baku.</li><li>On December 16, 2025, he was honored by the Mufti of Egypt and Chairman of the General Secretariat of the World Fatwa Houses and Institutions Prof. Nazir Muhammad Eyyad for his great contributions to religious and intellectual work, as well as for his efforts in promoting the values ​​of tolerance, moderation and intercultural dialogue, with the participation of muftis and great scholars from 50 countries of the world.</li><li>On March 17, 2026, he was awarded the &quot;Seal of the Prophet&quot; order in Egypt for his effective work in the field of service to science and knowledge, promotion of the values ​​of tolerance, and important contributions to the strengthening of friendly relations between nations.</li></ul></div><div class="card-resources"><a class="btn btn-primary" href="seymur-nasirov-media.html">Additional resources <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 6l6 6-6 6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></div>

Before

<p class="bio bio-lead">Professor Akif Suleymanov is a well-known lawyer and scientist in the field of constitutional law and public administration. He has the degrees of Doctor of Philosophy in Law (Ph.D.) and Doctor of Legal Sciences. His research is mainly devoted to theoretical and practical aspects of interaction between the President of Kazakhstan and the Constitutional Council and public control over executive authorities.</p><p class="bio">Professor Suleymanov, who has more than twenty years of academic experience, worked in pedagogical and administrative positions in a number of prestigious higher education institutions of Kazakhstan - Academy of Economics and Law, National Pedagogical University named after Abay, Narkhoz University and Turan University, where he currently works.</p><p class="bio">He is the author or co-author of 2 textbooks and 8 textbooks on public administration, constitutionalism, public control, human and civil rights. More than 100 scientific articles have been published as a result of his research on constitutional law, public control, gender policy and the political system of Kazakhstan. 6 of these articles are published in prestigious international scientific journals indexed in "Scopus." Also, his scientific writings were published in journals approved by the Higher Attestation Commissions of Kazakhstan and CIS countries, as well as in prestigious scientific publications of countries both nearby and farther afield.</p><p class="bio">In addition to his scientific activities, Professor Suleymanov, who actively participates in the field of public administration, is a member of the expert and advisory councils of the People&#x27;s Assembly of Kazakhstan, the Constitutional Court and the Fund for the Development of Parliamentarianism.</p><p class="bio">For his scientific achievements and public services, he was awarded the Birlik gold medal, as well as honorary decrees of the Ministry of Justice and Education of the Republic of Kazakhstan. In addition, he works as a member of the editorial boards of a number of scientific journals in the field of law in Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">He completed his undergraduate and postgraduate studies at the Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics of the Moscow State University named after M. V. Lomonosov.</p><p class="bio">He is a well-known Soviet, Russian and Azerbaijani scientist in the field of development of mathematical models and methods for the study of wave and oscillation processes in the creation of piezoelectric devices and apparatus used in the world ocean and outer space research, marine seismic exploration, electronics, defense and medical industries.</p><p class="bio">For the first time, he managed to solve the problem of determining the optimal shape of piezoelectric elements, which has not been solved for many years, meets the physical properties required in the dynamic mode, and has a minimum mass or volume. The solution to this problem made it possible to determine the location and individual characteristics of objects moving under water in the world ocean, the information of interest to experts in relevant scientific fields was recorded from space objects - artificial satellites and spaceships, and the creation of receiver-transmitter devices to transmit and receive the Flight Control Center. For the first time, he successfully applied the method of solving two- and three-dimensional dynamic problems, which are important in the creation of piezoelectric devices used in military equipment. The existence of the &quot;edge effect&quot; in disk-shaped piezoceramic membranes was also theoretically discovered by him for the first time. The piezoceramic actuator, developed jointly with the co-authors, was successfully used to solve the problem of creating an artificial heart. He is the author of more than 450 open and closed (confidential) scientific works, inventions, monographs, higher education textbooks, a number of scientific articles on the problems of organizing higher professional education and educational technologies. Under his scientific guidance, 7 graduate students, including 3 Azerbaijanis, defended their candidate dissertations. In general, based on the obtained scientific results, he delivered more than 60 presentations, including 12 commissioned plenary presentations, at 30 international and general congresses, conferences and symposia.</p><p class="bio">Some of the prizes and awards received by Professor Aladdin Allahverdiyev for his achievements in the fields of science, technology and education:</p><p class="bio">Medal named after the Hero of Socialist Labor of the Russian Cosmonautics Federation, lieutenant general, Lenin Prize laureate, professor, chairman of the State Commission on Space Programs Georgy Alexandrovich Tyulin;</p><p class="bio">Medal named after Khalil Ahmadovich Rakhmatulin, Hero of Socialist Labor of the National Committee for Theoretical and Applied Mechanics of the Russian Academy of Sciences, academician, laureate of four Orders of Lenin, several State Prizes;</p><p class="bio">the title &quot;Honored worker of higher vocational education of the Russian Federation&quot;;</p><p class="bio">Three times - in 1975, 1977 and 1980 - badges of &quot;The winner of the race of socialism&quot; established by the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, the former Council of Ministers of the USSR, the Central Committee of Trade Unions, the Central Committee of the All-Union Labor Party;</p><p class="bio">&quot;850th anniversary of Moscow&quot; state medal;</p><p class="bio">Jubilee medal &quot;250th anniversary of MSU named after M.V. Lomonosov&quot;;</p><p class="bio">Gold medal of the All-Russian Exhibition Center;</p><p class="bio">diploma of the winner of the review-competition of the Presidium of the Central Office of the All-Union Scientific Medical-Technical Society;</p><p class="bio">Laureate titles and cash prizes for 4 consecutive years (2001–2004) of the &quot;Moscow Grant&quot; competition established by the Moscow Government for science and technology in the field of education;</p><p class="bio">Numerous honorary decrees, diplomas, certificates, and other honors from the Russian Federation, several foreign countries, and many international institutions and organizations.</p>
